text:
calvin: Heads up — spotted a noisy partner flow (partner-42). They blast embeddings in short spikes and it trips global autoscale. Proposing per-API-key burst windows + weighted token accounting for internal/partner keys. Sketch below, PTAL.

maya: Can you paste the rate graph / sample logs so we can see shape?

calvin: Putting a quick sketch of the policy I'm thinking:

```
policy {
  key_id: "partner-42"
  burst_tokens: 2000           // tokens allowed instantly in burst window
  sustained_rps: 150          // steady-state request rate
  burst_window_s: 30          // time window where burst_tokens apply
  route_weights: { "embeddings": 3, "generation": 1 }
  schedule: optional { start: "00:00Z", end: "00:10Z" } // for scheduled sync windows
  override_meta: { created_by: "ops", reason: "migration sync", expires_at: "2026-04-01T00:00:00Z" }
  enforcement: "edge"  // enforce on edge node, fallback = 429
}
```

jordan: Security notes — need audit trail for any override, ability to rollback / revoke instantly, and principle-of-least-privilege for who can create overrides. Also want audit events forwarded to SIEM.

sarah: Product POV — if we expose "partner overrides" in Console we need explicit TTLs and a visible approval chain. Partners will ask for long-lived or permanent bursts; we should gate that behind sales/legal/contracts.

li: partner-ops here — partner-42 says their load is only during nightly sync windows. A scheduled burst window would solve their problem and reduce risk. Can we accept scheduled bursts instead of open-ended overrides?

calvin: Agree scheduled windows are cleaner. Also proposing an API-only path for override creation with fields: `override_reason`, `expires_at`, `requested_by` and an `internal_only` flag so partners can't self-serve console overrides.

devops-bot: deploybot: started rollout of feature branch `key-burst-config` to staging (canary 10% nodes).

maya: Enforcement question — cheap edge checks (token buckets) vs centralized counters (redis). Central is accurate but adds latency/cross-node ops. Suggest: approximate leaky buckets on edge + periodic reconciliation to central telemetry.

calvin: Exactly. Edge enforcement should be fast and approximate. Central telemetry aggregates weighted token usage for billing and observability. Need to make sure RouteWeights are applied both for enforcement (to throttle heavy ops earlier) and billing (to bill fairly).

jordan: Also require that any override creation emits an `override.created` event with key_id, who, ip, reason, expiry. Add a `revoke_override` quick action in Console that triggers immediate revocation.

sarah: UX ask — per-key card in Console with current RPS, burst remaining, active overrides (who/why/expiry), and a history timeline. That will make partner conversations much smoother.

li: We also need webhook hooks so partner-ops can be notified when a scheduled window starts/ends and when limits are approaching.

calvin: Next steps I propose: 1) I’ll open a design PR with schema + edge enforcement plan, 2) @maya run perf tests in staging canary, 3) @jordan add audit event spec and revoke action, 4) @sarah draft partner override contract text and Console mockups, 5) partner-ops own webhook/notify requirements.

maya: :thumbsup: I can validate perf tomorrow morning and post numbers here.

jordan: +1 — adding audit hooks to backlog and will specify SIEM fields.

sarah: I’ll start a short doc for partner SLAs and TTL guidance.

li: Thanks — if we can get scheduled windows + webhooks this will close the case for partner-42.

calvin: Thanks everyone. I’ll file the GH issue and link the PR here once it's up.
